To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the L_IR-T relation can be explained by a limited size of dusty starburst regions in high-z galaxies, and that the current interferometric observations of high-z dusty star forming galaxies are not yet of sufficient resolution.
the observed $L_{IR}-T$ relation is simply due the limited sizes of the DSBSRs in high-z starbursts.

the observed LIR-T relation is due to the limited sizes of the DSBSRs, which are smaller than ~2 kpc, and that the LIR-T relation outlines a boundary of the zone of avoidance in terms of the lower limits to minSFR3Ds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the limited R_eff of high-z dusty starbursts, and the resulting L_IR-T relation.
the physical properties of the DSBR, which is the most important part of the star formation process in galaxies.
the physical sizes of the DSB regions in high-z dusty star-forming galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed L-IR-T relation is simply the consequence of the limited sizes of DSBRs at high redshift.
the $L$-$T$ relation at high-z is simply due to limited R_eff.
the observed L(IR)-T relation is simply due the limited size of the DSBR in high-z galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed $L_{IR}$$-T$ relation is a result of the limited sizes of the DSBRS at high-z, and that the "zone of avoidances" can be used as a diagnostic tool to probe the physical conditions in the DSBR.
the L_IR-T relation can be understood as the result of a combination of the limited sizes and the limited SFR densities of the DSBR in the host galaxies.
the observed $L_{IR}^{\rm (cd)}-T$ relation can be interpreted as a consequence of the limited sizes of the DSBSRs at high-z.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L_IR-T relation can provide us with a direct measurement of the size of the DSBR, and thus the lower limits to minSFR3d, which are otherwise not easily accessible.
the L_IR-T relation at high-z can be used to estimate the sizes of the DSB regions, and hence the volume densities of star formation, of the host galaxies.
R_eff can be a good proxy of the DSBR size.
